verdicts.title: Query-to-Communication Lifting Using Low-Discrepancy Gadgets
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Lifting theorems are theorems that relate the query complexity of a function $f:\{0,1\}^{n}\to\{0,1\}$ to the communication complexity of the composed function $f \circ g^{n}$, for some "gadget" $g:\{0,1\}^{b}\times\{0,1\}^{b}\to\{0,1\}$. Such theorems allow transferring lower bounds from query complexity to the communication complexity, and have seen numerous applications in the recent years. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract proves lifting theorems via low-discrepancy gadgets of logarithmic length, not via tensor-amplified inner-product gadgets analyzed through asymptotic dimension/coarse geometry, and gives no log_2(k+1) per-query-bit bound tied to AsdimCertify multiplicity. It shares the lifting framework but does not interact with the specific CGL/asdim claim.

verdicts.title: A strong direct product theorem for quantum query complexity
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We show that quantum query complexity satisfies a strong direct product theorem. This means that computing $k$ copies of a function with less than $k$ times the quantum queries needed to compute one copy of the function implies that the overall success probability will be exponentially small in $k$. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns a strong direct product theorem for quantum query complexity via adversary methods, not deterministic two-party communication complexity of lifted functions, asymptotic dimension, or coarse geometric gadget composition. It shares the 'k copies' framing but does not interact with the specific CLC/asdim claim.

verdicts.title: A Lifting Theorem for Hybrid Classical-Quantum Communication Complexity
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We investigates a model of hybrid classical-quantum communication complexity, in which two parties first exchange classical messages and subsequently communicate using quantum messages. We study the trade-off between the classical and quantum communication for composed functions of the form $f\circ G^n$, where $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ and $G$ is an inner product function of $Θ(\log n)$ bits.
